summary.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover hit a record INR552.7 crore (+34.63% YoY) and PAT rose 38.49% to INR77.75 crore; FY26 turnover INR1,208.63 crore (+12.52%).
summary.overview: Mishra Dhatu Nigam reported its highest-ever quarterly turnover of INR552.7 crore in Q4 FY26, with value of production up 19.15% to INR392.19 crore and PBT up 38.67% to INR107 crore. For FY26, turnover reached INR1,208.63 crore (+12.52%) and PAT INR130.79 crore (+18.82%). Management highlighted record titanium output of about 700 tonnes, an order book of about INR2,290 crore as of April 1, 2026, and new qualifications (NADCAP heat treatment, CEMILAC airworthiness for 10 alloys). Management guided to roughly 15% top-line growth in FY27 with a 20% ambition, and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, conditional on raw material and energy (LPG) supply stabilising.

financial_highlights.change: Management also cited INR85 crore export done in FY26; figures differ in call

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 15% expected, with a 20% ambition dependent on raw material and energy supply.
EBITDA margin expected at about 23-25% (CFO-level comment cited 24-25%); PAT growth expected around 20%.
Open order book about INR2,250 crore; management expects about INR1,500 crore of new orders booked in FY27.
Metal bank expected to be established in about 4 months, with 3-4 months more needed for material receipt.
Inventory (WIP and scrap) targeted to fall 10-15% from opening levels.
Long-term 5-7 year ambition of INR5,000 crore top line cited, with 15-20% annual growth described as achievable; INR2,000 crore target seen as possibly achievable sooner than 3 years.
MOU targets for next year still under discussion with the Ministry.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of about INR1,000 crore over the next 3 years, mainly downstream forging and bar/wire equipment to replace machines installed around 1980-85; DPRs in progress, Board approval expected in 1-2 months, with more clarity by end FY27.
Funding preference: operating lease and term loans, with balance via working capital.
Metal bank (perpetual, for 6 critical raw materials) under civil works; establishment expected in about 4 months.
New vacuum arc remelting furnace installed; titanium capacity said to exceed the ~700 tonne FY26 output; titanium orders above INR660 crore in hand.
Aerospace fastener facility inaugurated, worth about INR40 crore, operational.
Spring plant for Vande Bharat being set up with an external subcontractor, expected to be fully operational in 1-2 months.
Powder manufacturing facility delayed by licence and dual-use clearance; purchase order placed, facility not yet installed; clarity expected next quarter.
demand_pricing: Open order book INR2,249-2,250 crore, of which defence is about 79%.
Titanium and maraging steel have higher margins than superalloys, per management; alloy-wise gross margins not disclosed.
Titanium orders above INR660 crore currently in hand.
Engine majors auditing facilities; commercial supplies expected towards end FY27 at earliest.
AMCA alloys (superalloys and titanium) under development; production orders expected once development completes.
ABHED bullet-proof jacket: one order of about INR1 crore executed for OCTOPUS; further orders anticipated.
Fixed-price contracts: management says raw material risk is priced into quotes; no price variation clause in fixed-price defence contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 see 20% top-line growth and 23% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 15% top-line growth (20% ambition), subject to raw material and LPG/energy stability. Margins expected at 23-25% EBITDA, with ~20% bottom-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What order inflow to expect by end FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,500 crore of orders expected to be booked in FY27 against an open order book of about INR2,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from products and by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 split: defence about INR301 crore, PSUs INR603 crore, space INR93 crore, energy INR2 crore, others INR129 crore, exports INR78 crore. Product-wise split not given as orders depend on customers.

qa_highlights.question: Alloy-wise gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose margins by alloy, calling it confidential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the metal bank and how is price risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal bank is a perpetual stock of 6 critical raw materials for customers, drawn only in emergencies; fixed-price contracts carry no price variation and pricing covers uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Fastener plant economics?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR40 crore facility is operational, serving missile and space; management expects at least INR20-30 crore order book per year, and a stable base of at least INR25 crore per year.

risks_watch: Raw material supply: India imports all key high-purity inputs (nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, tungsten, chromium, vanadium, rhenium), mainly from Europe, with titanium sponge from Kazakhstan; supply and sanctions risks persist.
Energy: LPG and energy issues linked to the Middle East and European crises could delay orders.
Fixed-price defence contracts with no price variation clause expose margins to alloy price spikes.
Powder facility licence and dual-use clearance still pending.
Export and engine-major orders depend on long audit cycles (expected towards end FY27).
Management did not give alloy-wise margins or product-wise revenue splits, limiting visibility.
Inventory build-up (WIP and scrap) to be reduced by 10-15%.
MOU targets with the Ministry not yet fixed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on achievements and FY27 growth, but cautious on raw material and energy constraints, which management repeatedly flagged as the binding variable. Evasive on alloy-wise margins, product revenue split and specific FY27 order sizes for springs and powder, deferring these to the next call.
